prompt:
Implement `parse` (src/parser.rs) for this INI crate, and make the `Ini` API behave as described below. Input is processed line by line: lines are separated by `\n`, a trailing `\r` is ignored, and line numbers start at 1.

1. Blank (or whitespace-only) lines are ignored. A line whose first non-whitespace character is `;` or `#` is a comment.
2. A line whose trimmed text starts with `[` is a section header. After removing an inline comment (rule 6) and trimming, it must end with `]`, and the name between the brackets, trimmed, must be non-empty and contain no `[` or `]`. Otherwise the error is `InvalidSectionHeader`. Section names are case-insensitive: they are stored and returned in lowercase. A section that appears again later continues the same section.
3. Every other line is `key = value`, split at the first `=`. No `=` is a `MissingEquals` error. The key is trimmed and case-sensitive; an empty key is an `EmptyKey` error. Keys that come before any section header belong to the section `""` (empty string).
4. Values are trimmed. If a key appears more than once in a section, the last value wins.
5. Quoted values: if the value (after leading whitespace) starts with `"`, it extends to the next unescaped `"`. Inside quotes, `\"`, `\\`, `\n` and `\t` are escapes for a quote, backslash, newline and tab; any other backslash is kept literally along with the character after it. The quoted content is not trimmed, and `;` / `#` inside it are ordinary characters. After the closing quote, the rest of the line may only be whitespace and/or a comment starting with `;` (here no whitespace is needed before the `;`); anything else is a `TrailingCharacters` error. No closing quote on the line is an `UnterminatedQuote` error.
6. Inline comments: in an unquoted value or a section header line, a `;` immediately preceded by a space or tab (in the original line) starts a comment that runs to the end of the line, so `k = ; note` gives an empty value. A `;` with no whitespace before it is ordinary text (`a=b;c` gives `b;c`), and `#` never starts an inline comment.
7. `Ini::sections()` lists section names in order of first appearance, each once. `""` is included (first) only if at least one key appears before the first header. A header with no keys still counts as a section.
8. `Ini::get(section, key)` matches the section name case-insensitively and the key exactly.
9. `parse` stops at the first error and returns `ParseError { line, kind }` with that line's number.

No dependencies; `cargo test --offline` must pass.
